news.story: Demin returned from a six-game absence due to a right leg bone bruise and turned in a productive performance on the offensive end. The second-year guard got to the charity stripe often and caught fire from deep, finishing with a season-high-tying 22 points. After scoring single-digit points in three of his first four regular-season appearances before missing the next six games, Demin will look to carry this momentum forward.

news.headline: Demin (leg) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Brian Lewis of the New York Post reported earlier Tuesday that Demin practiced as well. Demin was previously sidelined by a right leg bone bruise, but this designation suggests he is trending toward returning to Brooklyn's backcourt Wednesday. If he is cleared to play, the guard would be in position to reclaim the top spot at point guard.

His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.story: Acuff kept up his remarkable rookie production, finishing as Sacramento's second-leading scorer behind Zach LaVine and giving the Kings a steady source of offense all night. His scoring pace over 11 games is the best by a rookie since Michael Jordan in 1984, which is incredibly impressive given the cavalcade of rookie talent that came before him.

news.headline: Young finished Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons with 37 points (8-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 17-17 FT), 14 assists and two rebounds across 45 minutes.
news.story: Young struggled from two-point range, but he was productive from downtown and didn't miss a shot at the charity stripe, finishing with a team- and season-high scoring total. The star floor general also dished out a game- and season-best 14 assists, securing his fifth double-double of the campaign. The 28-year-old has reached the 20-point mark in three of his last five outings and has knocked down at least three triples in four of them.

news.headline: Young ended with 20 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-9 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

news.story: Clingan posted a double-double while adding two blocks. The young center wasn't as efficient as usual, but his size made a difference in the paint, especially against Domantas Sabonis. Clingan will have a tough matchup in Minnesota early next week.

news.headline: Clingan totaled seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win over Oklahoma City.
news.story: Clingan didn't score much, but he controlled the glass and protected the rim against an undersized Thunder frontcourt. That's exactly the role Portland needs from him, and he'll be a matchup problem for Oklahoma City again Wednesday.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. VanVleet did get held out for the second game of a back-to-back during that period, something that will likely continue to happen all season. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: VanVleet finished with 12 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), a rebound and two assists across 30 minutes in Monday's 110-100 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet provided efficient perimeter shooting but struggled to contribute beyond scoring, recording just two assists and no defensive stats. The limited playmaking was disappointing for fantasy managers. VanVleet's three-point production still offers value, but his fantasy reliability depends on generating more assists and steals. Staying under the 20-point threshold with subpar numbers in other categories simply won't cut it in standard leagues.

The superstar point guard has been on a tear, averaging 41.6 points, 7.8 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 2.9 combined steals-plus-blocks in 36.3 minutes per game over his last nine appearances. The star forward saw his streak of games with at least 20 points snap at four, but his consistent involvement on offense, both as a scorer and playmaker, gives him a strong floor until further notice.

news.headline: Siakam supplied 28 points (7-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 12-12 FT), eight rebounds, five assists and one steal across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 114-101 win over Washington.

The star forward was also second on the Pacers in rebounds and dished out at least five assists for a third straight game. He's reached the 20-point threshold in four consecutive contests, shooting 53.1 percent from the field over that stretch.

While his scoring was modest, he continues to provide the Lakers with a reliable interior presence alongside Luka Doncic (ankle) and Austin Reaves (heel). Kessler's rebounding and shot-blocking upside make him a solid option in standard leagues, particularly for those in need of big-man stats.

news.headline: Kessler recorded 21 points (8-12 FG, 5-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Monday's 124-114 victory over the Hawks.
news.story: Kessler was efficient around the rim and posted his sixth double-double over the past seven games. He scored at least 20 points for the third time this year and the first time since back-to-back such performances to begin the campaign. His rebounding and efficiency have made him one of the more pleasant surprises in fantasy so far, even on a night when his shot-blocking was quieter than usual.

news.headline: Herro had 18 points (5-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), two assists, two steals, one rebound and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 107-99 loss to the Magic.
news.story: Herro struggled mightily with efficiency Friday, but he still finished as Milwaukee's second-leading scorer. The star guard also tied the game-high mark in steals, chipping in multiple swipes for just the second time this season. He's scored at least 18 points in three of his last four outings, though he's shot just 25.0 percent from deep over that stretch.

news.headline: Herro had 27 points (8-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), seven assists, two rebounds and one block across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 123-112 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: Herro returned from a one-game absence due to a right knee contusion and immediately made an impact. The star guard turned in an efficient performance from inside the arc and led the Bucks in scoring and assists. He's reached the 20-point mark in four of his last five appearances, dishing out at least seven dimes in two of those outings.

news.headline: Herro (knee) is listed as available for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Herro didn't play in Tuesday's loss to the Knicks, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. However, he will play Wednesday, meaning Ryan Rollins will presumably return to the bench.

news.story: Vassell has been cleared to suit up and should provide San Antonio with a reliable perimeter scoring option against the Warriors. Through 10 games, he's averaging 11.9 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.1 assists.

news.headline: Vassell is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left adductor tightness.
news.story: Vassell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence with the issue. Julian Champagnie would likely draw a third straight start at power forward for the Spurs on Friday if Vassell is unable to play.

news.story: Wednesday marks a second consecutive absence for Vassell due to an adductor injury. His void in the starting lineup paves the way for Julian Champagnie to draw a second straight start on the wing for the Spurs.

news.headline: Peterson finished with 28 points (9-20 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 6-7 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: Peterson led Utah in scoring while knocking down four triples and contributing across multiple categories. The rookie guard attempted a team-high 20 shots, highlighting his prominent offensive role despite the defeat. Although his efficiency from beyond the arc left room for improvement, Peterson's combination of scoring volume, rebounding and defensive production makes him an intriguing fantasy option as he continues to develop.

news.headline: Peterson finished with 22 points (7-19 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 123-108 loss to the Magic.
news.story: This was Peterson's fourth straight 20-plus-point performance, and he again led his team in shot attempts. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) set to miss at least the next month, there's a massive hole to fill in Utah's offense, but Peterson looks ready to step into a larger role offensively.

news.headline: Peterson fouled out of Tuesday's 115-109 loss to the Heat after recording 25 points (10-19 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 31 minutes.
news.story: Peterson came close to posting a new career high yet again after scoring his season-high 26 Tuesday, and the rookie is starting to look comfortable as Utah's go-to scorer. The turnovers and fouls are still part of the learning curve, but with three starters out, the Jazz are giving him all the touches he can handle. Utah hosts Orlando on Wednesday to finish a back-to-back.

news.headline: Camara contributed 14 points (5-7 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals across 36 minutes during Friday's 120-107 victory over Sacramento.
news.story: Camara gave Portland a quiet but efficient 14 points in 36 minutes. He'll never be the Blazers' top option, but his defensive skill set makes him one of the team's most valuable role players. With Portland down two key guards, his minutes should stay high.

news.headline: Camara accumulated 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 30 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: Camara was Portland's most efficient scorer Friday, hitting half of his three-point attempts while also doing the defensive work the Blazers count on. When he's making shots from the corner, Portland's starting lineup gets much harder to guard. He's a key piece of the rotation, and nights like this show why he's playing starter minutes.

news.headline: Pritchard finished Wednesday's 98-93 win over the Raptors with 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one assist and one rebound over 31 minutes.
news.story: The Celtics' offense looked sluggish on the second leg of a back-to-back set, not to mention that they were without Paul George (illness) for Wednesday's contest. Pritchard wasn't the most efficient from the field, but he led the Celtics' bench in scoring and finished third on the team in points behind Jayson Tatum (24) and Derrick White (19). Pritchard has scored in double digits in each of his last five games, and over that span he has connected on 43.8 percent of his three-point attempts on 6.4 3PA/G while averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 assists and 3.8 rebounds over 26.3 minutes.

news.headline: Pritchard finished Tuesday's 123-101 win over Philadelphia with 18 points (7-15 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and one steal in 30 minutes.
news.story: Pritchard delivered an efficient all-around performance off the bench, connecting on four three-pointers while adding solid rebounding and playmaking production. His consistent involvement in Boston's backcourt continues to support his fantasy appeal. He's scored in double digits in a season-long four consecutive games, averaging 13.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game over that stretch.

news.headline: Pritchard tallied 12 points (4-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and a steal across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Pritchard made all four of his field goals from beyond the arc to snap an 0-for-12 drought from three in his previous three contests. Inconsistency has been Pritchard's biggest issue so far. He has failed to score more than 12 points in four straight games, but he's also surpassed the 25-point mark twice already. At the end of the day, while his ability to produce across multiple categories remains encouraging, Pritchard's fantasy outlook still depends on his perimeter shooting as his primary source of production.

news.headline: McCain recorded 23 points (8-17 FG, 7-11 3Pt), four rebounds and two assists in 31 minutes during Friday's 113-112 loss to the Clippers.
news.story: McCain caught fire from deep, hitting seven of his 11 three-point attempts. He's been thrust into a bigger role with so many Thunder players hurt, and he's starting to look comfortable as a secondary option behind Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Oklahoma City badly needs his shooting while it waits to get healthy.

news.story: Queta led the Celtics in rebounds Wednesday and made two clutch free throws late in the fourth quarter to extend Boston's lead to three points. It was the first double-double of the 2026-27 campaign for Queta, who has started in each of the Celtics' last seven games in place of Mitchell Robinson. In that seven-game span, Queta has averaged 9.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.1 blocks over 24.6 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Queta posted 13 points (6-11 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds and four assists across 22 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Queta narrowly missed a double-double while contributing four assists, an encouraging development for a player whose fantasy value typically centers on rebounding and interior scoring. Queta will remain a valuable fantasy option as long as he remains the Celtics' No. 1 option at center ahead of Mitchell Robinson, who also posted a strong fantasy line Sunday with 12 points (6-6 FG, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block across 18 minutes.

news.headline: Queta racked up nine points (4-8 FG, 1-3 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Queta is staking his claim for the top center role in Boston, starting three consecutive games and coming down with a season-high 12 boards Wednesday. He's played at least 26 minutes each time out during this period, which is enough playing time to make Queta worth rostering in most fantasy leagues.

news.headline: Robinson delivered 12 points (6-6 FG, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block across 18 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Robinson produced exceptional defensive value in limited action and was efficient on offense, scoring in double digits for just the second time this season. While he's losing the battle for the Celtics' starting center spot to Neemias Queta, Robinson has excellent per-minute production. His rebounding, defensive production and field-goal efficiency make him intriguing in category formats, though his limited workload and free-throw struggles remain significant negatives.

news.story: Robinson popped up on the injury report due to an illness. However, it won't keep him off the floor against Milwaukee. Robinson's presence will likely mean fewer minutes for Luka Garza.

news.story: Robinson isn't feeling well and may not be available against the Bucks, which would mark his second absence of the 2026-27 campaign. If Robinson can't suit up, it should mean more minutes for Luka Garza behind Neemias Queta.

It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. He's expected to miss a significant chunk of the 2026-27 season while recovering, but the Thunder should have a better idea of a timeline for his return following surgery.

news.story: Williams suffered a gruesome left ankle injury after crashing to the floor on a drive to the rim, resulting in him being taken off on a stretcher. A considerable layoff seems imminent for Williams, likely leaving minutes for Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Alex Caruso and Kenrich Williams to absorb.

news.headline: Mara amassed 10 points (5-6 FG), three rebounds and three blocks across 21 minutes during Friday's 113-112 loss to the Clippers.
news.story: Mara made his fourth start of the season as Oklahoma City again started two 7-footers, and he was efficient around the rim while blocking three shots. The rookie center's size has given the Thunder a different look with Chet Holmgren (knee) out. Mara is likely to keep starting alongside Isaiah Hartenstein for now.

news.headline: Mara is in the starting lineup for Wednesday's matchup with the Trail Blazers, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
news.story: Joining Mara in the first unit for Wednesday's game will be Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Alex Caruso and Isaiah Hartenstein. Over two starts this season, Mara is averaging 13.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 3.0 swats per contest.

news.headline: Mara had 10 points (5-9 FG, 0-1 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one block in 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 loss to Portland.
news.story: Mara gave the Thunder good minutes off the bench, finishing around the rim and holding his own on the glass. With Chet Holmgren (knee) and Jaylin Williams (back) out, the rookie center is getting a real chance to play. He'll split time with Isaiah Hartenstein for now, but performances like this make him hard to keep off the floor.

news.headline: Flagg chipped in 12 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and two steals over 27 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Flagg struggled to establish himself offensively, attempting only 12 shots as Dallas fell behind early and didn't recover. His seven rebounds and two steals helped preserve some fantasy value despite the modest scoring output, but fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about one bad game. Flagg has had some inconsistencies, but for the most part, his numbers have been excellent. He has surpassed the 20-point mark in seven of his 11 appearances, averaging 6.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.2 steals per contest.

news.headline: Flagg finished with 43 points (16-25 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 8-8 FT), 11 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block in 39 minutes during Monday's 125-122 win over Indiana.
news.story: Flagg delivered his best offensive showing of the 2026-27 season so far, beating his previous high of 33 points Oct. 30 against Houston. He also set a season high in rebounds and has now reached double-digit boards three times in 10 matchups. Flagg has now collected four straight double-doubles following Monday's victory.

news.headline: Acuff finished Friday's 120-107 loss to the Trail Blazers with 17 points (6-19 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
news.story: The rookie had to work for his 17 points Friday, needing 19 shots and going just 3-for-10 from deep, though he matched Zach LaVine for the team lead with six assists. Acuff has been handed a lot of responsibility on a struggling Kings team, and nights like this are part of the learning curve. Sacramento has now lost five straight and is still winless at home, so his minutes aren't going anywhere. Next up is a tough Sunday matchup with Oklahoma City.

news.story: Acuff kept up his remarkable rookie production, finishing as Sacramento's second-leading scorer behind Zach LaVine and giving the Kings a steady source of offense all night. His scoring pace over 11 games is the best by a rookie since Michael Jordan in 1984, which is incredibly impressive given the cavalcade of rookie talent that came before him.

news.headline: Clingan contributed 13 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 120-107 win over the Kings.
news.story: Clingan posted a double-double while adding two blocks. The young center wasn't as efficient as usual, but his size made a difference in the paint, especially against Domantas Sabonis. Clingan will have a tough matchup in Minnesota early next week.

news.headline: Clingan totaled seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win over Oklahoma City.
news.story: Clingan didn't score much, but he controlled the glass and protected the rim against an undersized Thunder frontcourt. That's exactly the role Portland needs from him, and he'll be a matchup problem for Oklahoma City again Wednesday.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

The second-year guard got to the charity stripe often and caught fire from deep, finishing with a season-high-tying 22 points. After scoring single-digit points in three of his first four regular-season appearances before missing the next six games, Demin will look to carry this momentum forward.

Demin was previously sidelined by a right leg bone bruise, but this designation suggests he is trending toward returning to Brooklyn's backcourt Wednesday. If he is cleared to play, the guard would be in position to reclaim the top spot at point guard.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. VanVleet did get held out for the second game of a back-to-back during that period, something that will likely continue to happen all season. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: VanVleet finished with 12 points (4-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 1-2 FT), a rebound and two assists across 30 minutes in Monday's 110-100 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet provided efficient perimeter shooting but struggled to contribute beyond scoring, recording just two assists and no defensive stats. The limited playmaking was disappointing for fantasy managers. VanVleet's three-point production still offers value, but his fantasy reliability depends on generating more assists and steals. Staying under the 20-point threshold with subpar numbers in other categories simply won't cut it in standard leagues.

news.headline: Zubac supplied 12 points (6-12 FG), 13 rebounds, one assist and one block in 26 minutes during Friday's 106-104 win over the Knicks.
news.story: That's now back-to-back double-doubles for Zubac, who appears to be just about all the way back from a recent extended absence due to an ankle sprain. news.headline: Queta recorded 11 points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 6-8 FT), 13 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and one steal over 31 minutes during the Celtics' 98-93 win over the Raptors on Wednesday.
news.story: Queta led the Celtics in rebounds Wednesday and made two clutch free throws late in the fourth quarter to extend Boston's lead to three points. It was the first double-double of the 2026-27 campaign for Queta, who has started in each of the Celtics' last seven games in place of Mitchell Robinson. In that seven-game span, Queta has averaged 9.3 points, 8.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.1 blocks over 24.6 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Queta posted 13 points (6-11 FG, 1-2 FT), nine rebounds and four assists across 22 minutes in Sunday's 117-97 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Queta narrowly missed a double-double while contributing four assists, an encouraging development for a player whose fantasy value typically centers on rebounding and interior scoring. Queta will remain a valuable fantasy option as long as he remains the Celtics' No. 1 option at center ahead of Mitchell Robinson, who also posted a strong fantasy line Sunday with 12 points (6-6 FG, 0-2 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and a block across 18 minutes.

news.headline: Queta racked up nine points (4-8 FG, 1-3 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 109-102 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Queta is staking his claim for the top center role in Boston, starting three consecutive games and coming down with a season-high 12 boards Wednesday. He's played at least 26 minutes each time out during this period, which is enough playing time to make Queta worth rostering in most fantasy leagues.

news.headline: Siakam posted 19 points (5-13 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 7-12 FT), three rebounds and two assists across 32 minutes in Friday's 106-104 win over the Knicks.
news.story: Siakam didn't have his best shooting performance, but seven attempts from the charity stripe allowed him to boost his scoring numbers en route to leading the Pacers to an upset win. The star forward saw his streak of games with at least 20 points snap at four, but his consistent involvement on offense, both as a scorer and playmaker, gives him a strong floor until further notice.

news.headline: Siakam supplied 28 points (7-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 12-12 FT), eight rebounds, five assists and one steal across 32 minutes in Wednesday's 114-101 win over Washington.
news.story: Siakam didn't deliver his most efficient shooting performance, though he got to the charity stripe frequently and finished with a game-high scoring total. The star forward was also second on the Pacers in rebounds and dished out at least five assists for a third straight game. He's reached the 20-point threshold in four consecutive contests, shooting 53.1 percent from the field over that stretch.

news.headline: Pritchard finished Wednesday's 98-93 win over the Raptors with 14 points (5-13 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one assist and one rebound over 31 minutes.
news.story: The Celtics' offense looked sluggish on the second leg of a back-to-back set, not to mention that they were without Paul George (illness) for Wednesday's contest. Pritchard wasn't the most efficient from the field, but he led the Celtics' bench in scoring and finished third on the team in points behind Jayson Tatum (24) and Derrick White (19). Pritchard has scored in double digits in each of his last five games, and over that span he has connected on 43.8 percent of his three-point attempts on 6.4 3PA/G while averaging 13.2 points, 4.0 assists and 3.8 rebounds over 26.3 minutes.

His consistent involvement in Boston's backcourt continues to support his fantasy appeal. He's scored in double digits in a season-long four consecutive games, averaging 13.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game over that stretch.

news.headline: Pritchard tallied 12 points (4-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt), six rebounds, five assists and a steal across 23 minutes in Friday's 119-80 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Pritchard made all four of his field goals from beyond the arc to snap an 0-for-12 drought from three in his previous three contests. At the end of the day, while his ability to produce across multiple categories remains encouraging, Pritchard's fantasy outlook still depends on his perimeter shooting as his primary source of production.

news.story: Camara gave Portland a quiet but efficient 14 points in 36 minutes. He'll never be the Blazers' top option, but his defensive skill set makes him one of the team's most valuable role players. With Portland down two key guards, his minutes should stay high.

news.headline: Camara accumulated 18 points (7-12 FG, 4-8 3Pt), six rebounds and one assist in 30 minutes during Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: Camara was Portland's most efficient scorer Friday, hitting half of his three-point attempts while also doing the defensive work the Blazers count on. news.headline: Herro had 18 points (5-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-7 FT), two assists, two steals, one rebound and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 107-99 loss to the Magic.

news.headline: Herro had 27 points (8-16 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 9-10 FT), seven assists, two rebounds and one block across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 123-112 loss to the Lakers.

news.headline: Herro (knee) is listed as available for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.

His two made three-pointers and perfect free-throw shooting strengthened his offensive efficiency, while his defensive contributions provided additional value. McDaniels remains particularly useful in category formats, where his versatility can compensate for inconsistent scoring volume.

news.headline: Edgecombe recorded 19 points (8-13 FG, 3-5 3Pt), three rebounds, two assists and four steals over 32 minutes in Friday's 119-95 loss to the Cavs.
news.story: Edgecombe was locked in on both ends of the floor, ripping away a season-high four steals while also scoring with remarkable efficiency. He also finished without committing a single turnover, which was nice to see after he coughed up the rock a season-high three times in his previous outing.

news.headline: Williams will start Monday's game against the Hawks.
news.story: With Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (finger) sidelined, Williams will join the first unit for the first time since Oct. 27. In four starts this season, he's averaged 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals across 28.5 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Williams accumulated eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Williams gave the Lakers useful minutes off the bench, knocking down a pair of three-pointers and picking up two steals in his 20 minutes. The forward missed three straight games with soreness in his left foot, an issue going back to the preseason, before being cleared to return earlier in the week. The Lakers begin a back-to-back Sunday, so he could be held out for one of those games.

news.headline: Williams contributed 10 points (3-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), four rebounds, one assist and two steals in 23 minutes during Wednesday's 116-103 victory over the Kings.
news.story: After beginning the year as a starter, Williams seems to be getting eased back into action following a recent absence. He'll continue competing with Jake LaRavia for the Lakers' fifth starting lineup position.

signals.detail: For now, Reaves can be considered questionable for Sunday's game in Phoenix, and if he needs to miss that one, Ziaire Williams would likely return to the starting lineup.

news.headline: Reaves (heel) didn't participate in Saturday's practice, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Reaves sustained a bruised left heel in Wednesday's win over Milwaukee and is considered day-to-day, though this update is not encouraging ahead of Sunday's game against Phoenix. If the 28-year-old guard is unable to suit up, Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes (finger) and Collin Sexton (head) would be candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Reaves (heel) won't undergo imaging and is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Suns, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
news.story: An official designation for Reaves' status will be given Saturday, according to Buha, and head coach JJ Redick also said Reaves has a bruise on his heel. The star guard is enjoying an excellent start to the season and is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game. If he's sidelined, expect Ziaire Williams to start in the backcourt alongside Luka Doncic.

news.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said that X-rays on Reaves' left heel came back negative, but they won't have another update until he undergoes further imaging back in Los Angeles on Thursday, Dave McMenamin of ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Reaves hurt his heel coming down after a layup attempt, but the good news is that an Achilles injury has been ruled out. The Lakers are off until Sunday, but if Reaves needs to miss that game, Ziaire Williams would have a chance to start and Luka Doncic would be extremely busy on offense.

news.headline: Smith (finger) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game at Minnesota.
news.story: Smith is in jeopardy of missing Saturday's contest after aggravating his sprained left finger in Friday's overtime win over Atlanta. With Nic Claxton (hamstring) also questionable, the Bulls could be shorthanded in the frontcourt. If either of those guys is ruled out, Zach Collins would likely see increased burn.

news.headline: Smith (hand) exited Friday's 125-117 win over the Hawks in overtime and did not return, finishing with 15 points (6-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals across 32 minutes.
news.story: Smith secured his third double-double of the season while tying his season-high mark in steals. However, the big man came down on his left hand in overtime and exited to the locker room. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's game at Minnesota.

news.headline: Smith exited to the locker room in overtime during Friday's game against the Hawks due to an apparent left hand injury, Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Smith went back to the locker room holding his left hand. The big man can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

signals.detail: With Andrew Wiggins already in line to fill in for Pelle Larsson (illness) on Friday, rookie second-rounder Ryan Conwell could be preparing for his first career start.

news.headline: Thompson (ankle) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against the Pistons.
news.story: Thompson missed the front end of this back-to-back set due to a left ankle sprain, though he's trending toward playing Saturday. If the veteran sharpshooter is cleared to play, there would be fewer minutes available for the likes of Ryan Conwell, Tim Hardaway and Myron Gardner.

news.headline: Thompson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Cavaliers.
news.story: The Heat sent mixed signals regarding the status of Thompson, first listing him as probable and later questionable before ruling him out altogether. With Andrew Wiggins already in line to fill in for Pelle Larsson (illness) on Friday, rookie second-rounder Ryan Conwell could be preparing for his first career start.

news.headline: Thompson (ankle) has been downgraded to questionable for Friday's game against Cleveland.
news.story: Thompson initially drew a questionable tag before being upgraded to probable, though he's now trending in the wrong direction ahead of tipoff at 8:00 p.m. ET. If the veteran sharpshooter joins Pelle Larsson (illness) on the inactive list, Tim Hardaway, Ryan Conwell and Andrew Wiggins would be candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear due to an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

news.headline: Markkanen is out for Tuesday's game versus the Heat with a right wrist sprain.
news.story: The star forward is missing a second consecutive contest, and he faces a short turnaround to return ahead of Wednesday's tilt against the Magic. Josh Green figures to draw a second straight start, while Brice Sensabaugh and Josh Okogie should see a bump in playing time.

news.headline: Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Tuesday's game against Miami.
news.story: Markkanen was held out Sunday due to a right wrist sprain, but the fact that he's been upgraded to questionable is a positive sign. Utah should have another update on the forward's availability closer to tipoff.

news.headline: Expert fantasy hoops roundtable: Is Wemby No. 1? Plus early surprises and more
news.story: A little over three weeks into the NBA season, we now have a good idea -- even if not a complete picture -- of what type of fantasy impact players are going to have this season. Has Luka Doncic's production gone up a whole different level without LeBron James in Los Angeles, as many expected? You bet he has. Has Cooper Flagg found another level in Year 2 in Dallas? No doubt. A closer look at the top five on the ESPN Player Rater heading into Wednesday's action reveals, in order: Victor Wembanyama, Doncic, Flagg, Tyrese Maxey and Nikola Jokic. news.headline: George (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Toronto, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
news.story: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Mavericks. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Sam Hauser and Hugo Gonzalez are all candidates to see increased playing time.

news.headline: George tallied 36 points (14-22 FG, 6-11 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds and one assist across 30 minutes during Tuesday's 123-101 win over Philadelphia.
news.story: George made his return to Philadelphia after being swapped for Jaylen Brown over the summer, as the former Sixer spent the previous two years there. George delivered masterfully with a game-high 36 points and six three-pointers, and he's now scored 25-plus points in three of his last four outings while shooting a scorching-hot 51.4 percent (18-for-35) from behind the arc over that stretch. Boston has now won four consecutive contests to improve to 9-2 on the season, and George's play certainly has a lot to do with that.

news.headline: Davis contributed 30 points (13-21 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 15 rebounds, four assists and one steal over 44 minutes before fouling out of Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Davis put together another strong performance despite ultimately fouling out, recording his fourth straight 20-and-10 game. Although the Washington win/loss record is not ideal, Davis appears motivated and, to this point, has been a first-round player in standard leagues. Through 11 games, he has averaged 25.6 points, 10.5 rebounds and 2.3 combined steals and blocks.

news.headline: Davis registered 44 points (16-21 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 10-11 FT), 13 rebounds, one assist and one steal in 34 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Davis, who missed his team's previous two matchups due to an ankle injury, wasted no time in proving his health Monday. He pieced together an incredibly efficient 40-plus point performance, needing only 21 attempts from the field to set his best scoring mark of the young season. Davis also crashed the boards to secure a double-double for the third time in his last four appearances.

signals.detail: Only rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who scored 25, had more points for the Warriors, but the other three members of the starting lineup combined for just 12.

news.headline: Podziemski had 22 points (7-15 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 4-5 FT), six rebounds, four assists and two steals across 37 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: Only rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who scored 25, had more points for the Warriors, but the other three members of the starting lineup combined for just 12. Podziemski has delivered at least 20 points in four of the last seven games, averaging 18.4 points, 5.3 boards, 4.0 assists, 3.4 threes and 1.3 steals over that span. The fourth-year guard could see his usage increase significantly with Stephen Curry (abdomen) slated to miss at least two weeks after an MRI revealed an abdominal tear.

news.headline: Podziemski totaled 25 points (10-19 FG, 5-11 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in 26 minutes during Monday's 138-87 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Podziemski teamed up with Stephen Curry to account for 50 points on the way to a blowout victory. The 23-year-old guard has looked sharp from downtown over his last two matchups, hitting nine of 16 attempts. His 25-point showing is his best of the season thus far through nine appearances.

news.headline: Podziemski finished with 15 points (5-7 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, an assist, two steals and a block across 39 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Podziemski delivered efficient perimeter shooting and valuable defensive production while playing a season-high 39 minutes, but with his workload sitting firmly at around 33 minutes per game, his role on offense is pretty much set in stone as a multi-category contributor who can hit threes. His scoring ceiling still depends on shot volume in Golden State's offense, but his contributions in other categories are a nice boost, even if they are inconsistent at times.

news.headline: Spencer provided 15 points (5-7 FG, 3-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), three rebounds, three assists and one block across 20 minutes during Wednesday's 123-118 loss to Denver.
news.story: Spencer had already overtaken Scotty Pippen (back) before the latter went down with an injury, and the former continues to supply deep-league fantasy appeal at point guard. Over his past six appearances, Spencer has averaged 9.8 points, 6.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 three-pointers while shooting a scorching 50.0 percent from beyond the arc.

news.story: Risers and Fallers is back this week with a look at three players who are on the rise and might be worth adding, along with three others who are struggling to the point of being potential drop candidates. I didn't write up Oklahoma City big man Aday Mara, but if you're in need of a center, Chet Holmgren is out for about three months and Mara simply has to play. I think he's going to have a big second half, and he's only rostered in 18.7% of ESPN leagues. news.headline: Coward finished with 15 points (5-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-4 FT), 11 rebounds and four assists over 27 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: This was Coward's third double-double of the season and the 10th of his career. He's been a top-40 producer this season with averages of 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 2.3 triples and 1.5 steals per game.

news.headline: Coward tallied 23 points (8-19 FG, 4-12 3Pt, 3-4 FT), nine rebounds, four assists and four steals over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
news.story: Coward was coming off back-to-back 10-point performances, but he was much more aggressive seeking out his own shot Wednesday and cracked the 20-point plateau for the first time this season. He'll look to keep his momentum going into Friday's meeting with the Thunder.

news.headline: Coward logged 10 points (3-6 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), nine rebounds and three assists over 31 minutes during Monday's 135-134 overtime loss to the Pelicans.
news.story: Coward fell just one rebound short of what would have been his third double-double of the season, although as a whole, this was a somewhat underwhelming performance. Despite some inconsistencies, Coward has cobbled together a strong start to the season, averaging 12.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.2 steals and 2.5 three-pointers, good enough for borderline top-50 value.

news.headline: Wolf registered 10 points (3-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, four assists, a steal and two blocks across 29 minutes in Wednesday's 145-111 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Wolf delivered a productive multi-category performance, securing a double-double for the second time in his last three starts while adding three combined defensive stats. His four assists were also valuable, highlighting his ability to contribute beyond traditional frontcourt categories. Wolf's rebounding and defensive activity provide an encouraging fantasy foundation, and his scoring seems to be trending in the right direction as well. This was his fourth consecutive game with 10 or more points. He'll be a valuable waiver pickup as long as he remains in the starting unit.

news.headline: Wolf accumulated 11 points (4-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 1-4 FT), 10 rebounds and one assist in 31 minutes during Saturday's 124-121 loss to the Hawks.
news.story: Wolf moved into the starting lineup as Brooklyn continues to tinker with its rotation. While it wasn't the best performance, Wolf did enough to keep himself on the radar as a short-term streaming asset. Brooklyn faces Dallas on Sunday, meaning anyone who picked up Wolf should hold him for at least one more game.

news.headline: Wolf will be in the starting lineup for Saturday's matchup with the Hawks, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Wolf hasn't been a consistent part of the rotation this season, but with the Nets 2-6 to begin the year, head coach Jordi Fernandez will look to shake up his starting lineup. Joining Wolf in the first unit for Saturday's game will be Nolan Traore, Michael Porter, Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe.

news.headline: Peterson finished with 28 points (9-20 FG, 4-11 3Pt, 6-7 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block across 34 minutes in Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: Peterson led Utah in scoring while knocking down four triples and contributing across multiple categories. The rookie guard attempted a team-high 20 shots, highlighting his prominent offensive role despite the defeat. Although his efficiency from beyond the arc left room for improvement, Peterson's combination of scoring volume, rebounding and defensive production makes him an intriguing fantasy option as he continues to develop.

news.headline: Peterson finished with 22 points (7-19 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block over 33 minutes in Wednesday's 123-108 loss to the Magic.
news.story: This was Peterson's fourth straight 20-plus-point performance, and he again led his team in shot attempts. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) set to miss at least the next month, there's a massive hole to fill in Utah's offense, but Peterson looks ready to step into a larger role offensively.

news.headline: Peterson fouled out of Tuesday's 115-109 loss to the Heat after recording 25 points (10-19 FG, 4-9 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 31 minutes.
news.story: Peterson came close to posting a new career high yet again after scoring his season-high 26 Tuesday, and the rookie is starting to look comfortable as Utah's go-to scorer. The turnovers and fouls are still part of the learning curve, but with three starters out, the Jazz are giving him all the touches he can handle. Utah hosts Orlando on Wednesday to finish a back-to-back.

news.headline: Wells accounted for 22 points (6-13 FG, 5-10 3Pt, 5-5 FT), two rebounds and one assist over 31 minutes in Wednesday's 123-118 loss to Denver.
news.story: Wells' hot streak continued Wednesday, as he set season highs in points and triples and drilled all five of his freebies. He's been shooting the lights out over his past two outings, pouring in 36 points and nine treys on 11-for-21 shooting from the field and 9-for-15 from distance. He'll look to keep his foot on the gas pedal Friday in New Orleans.

news.headline: Wells had zero points (0-3 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one block in 21 minutes during Wednesday's 107-103 loss to the Pacers.
news.story: Wells failed to convert any of his three attempts from beyond the arc and battled foul trouble, picking up five personal fouls. Despite retaining his starting role, he offered little offensive production while Cedric Coward and Ty Jerome carried Memphis' scoring load. Wells' limited contributions outside of scoring make nights like this particularly damaging to his fantasy value.

news.headline: Wells logged four points (2-5 FG, 0-3 3Pt), two rebounds and one steal over 22 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 win over Sacramento.
news.story: Wells had the opportunity to operate in an expanded role Saturday due to the absences of Ty Jerome (back) and Scotty Pippen (back). However, Wells attempted a season-low five field goals and failed to score in double digits for the first time in the 2026-27 season. Through six games in October, he averaged 12.2 points, 3.7 rebounds, 1.0 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.8 threes over 27.2 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Doncic (ankle) won't be listed on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Suns, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
news.story: The Lakers have yet to release their official injury report, though Doncic won't be included after exiting Wednesday's win over Milwaukee with an ankle injury. The superstar point guard has been on a tear, averaging 41.6 points, 7.8 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 2.9 combined steals-plus-blocks in 36.3 minutes per game over his last nine appearances. He's scored at least 32 points in all nine of those outings.

news.headline: Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Doncic (ankle) is "fine," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
news.story: The superstar guard exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's win over the Bucks due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return. Doncic can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable marker until the Lakers release an official injury report at some point prior to Sunday's matchup in Phoenix.

news.headline: Doncic finished Wednesday's 123-112 win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-25 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 7-10 FT), five rebounds, five assists and three steals across 32 minutes. He exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
news.story: Doncic didn't deliver his most efficient shooting effort, though he still led all players in scoring while knocking down a game-high-tying five triples. He has now reached the 30-point threshold in each of his last nine appearances. The superstar floor general also tied for the game-best mark in steals, logging multiple swipes for the fourth time over his last six outings. However, Doncic's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game at Phoenix, as he landed on Kyle Kuzma's foot and exited to the locker room Wednesday.

news.headline: Kessler logged 10 points (5-10 FG), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal over 29 minutes during Wednesday's 123-112 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: Kessler recorded another double-double, controlling the glass while adding a steal and a block. While his scoring was modest, he continues to provide the Lakers with a reliable interior presence alongside Luka Doncic (ankle) and Austin Reaves (heel). Kessler's rebounding and shot-blocking upside make him a solid option in standard leagues, particularly for those in need of big-man stats.

news.headline: Kessler recorded 21 points (8-12 FG, 5-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 30 minutes during Monday's 124-114 victory over the Hawks.
news.story: Kessler was efficient around the rim and posted his sixth double-double over the past seven games. He scored at least 20 points for the third time this year and the first time since back-to-back such performances to begin the campaign. His rebounding and efficiency have made him one of the more pleasant surprises in fantasy so far, even on a night when his shot-blocking was quieter than usual.
